newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU clears CLT/Bertelsmann's UFA merger.
newsitem.headline: EU clears CLT/Bertelsmann's UFA merger.

text.p: The European Commission said Monday it cleared the merger between Luxembourg-based broadcaster CLT and German media group Bertelsmann's television unit UFA.

The operation will create Europe's largest television alliance in terms of revenue. It will focus mainly on free-access TV after the two partners in September dropped plans to launch a digital pay-television channel in Germany.
After a routine one-month probe, the Commission concluded the operation would not lead to the creation of a dominant position even in Germany where the two partners are both active.
This was because they would face competition from commercial television channels linked to a rival group operated by Bavarian media mogul Leo Kirch.

The clearance of the alliance between the two strong media players came as little surprise after European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert said abandonment of their pay-television plans made the Commission's approval easier.
But it will come as a relief for the sector, which has suffered from a particularly tough Commission stance regarding media ventures in the past.
Under the terms of the agreement, CLT and UFA will be merged in a joint venture which will be jointly operated by Bertelsmann and Audiofina, which controls CLT.
CLT and UFA are already partners in a number of German TV operations including the country's largest commercial channel RTL.
The Commission in 1994 blocked a proposed joint venture between Bertelsmann, Kirch and Deutsche Telekom to provide services for pay-TV due to fears it would close the market for newcomers.
Last year, it also also banned two media joint ventures in the Netherlands and in the Nordic market.
